title: Henham Park (multiple incidents) 41-28590 Memorial

external_narratives.summary: IWM registers this memorial commemorating B-24 Liberators 42-110033 and 41-28590 of the 93rd Bomb Group USAAF. The two aircraft collided while forming up for a mission to Brunswick on 29 March 1944 and crashed onto the Henham estate.
external_narratives.link_description: Memorial honoring B-24 Liberators 42-110033 and 41-28590 in Henham Park from USAAF's 93rd Bomb Group.

external_narratives.summary: The American Air Museum records 42-110033 'Arizona Rambler' as a B-24H from the 330th Bomb Squadron, 93rd Bomb Group ('The Travelling Circus'). The aircraft collided with 41-28590 during assembly over Henham Park. Only three of the 20 airmen survived the initial crash, and a subsequent explosion during rescue operations killed 19 additional personnel from rescue, medical, and fire-fighting units at nearby Holton Airfield.
key_details: 19 rescue/medical/fire personnel also killed in secondary explosion

memorial_details:
Two black marble plaques, one horizontal and one upright. Upright stone has irregular shape with smooth front and is set on a base of slate chippings, surrounded by wooden fence. Upright: Commemorative inscription in white lettering below badge of USAAF 8th Air Force with silhouette of Liberator below. Coat of Arms of 6th Earl of Stradbroke alongside detail of memorial erection. Horizontal: Details of those who died.

The memorial was first erected in 1994 after a request from an airman who had missed a flight on one of the ill-fated B24 Liberators, as well as money from the Earl of Stradbroke at that time.

This memorial was erected by the 8th Earl of Stradbroke in 1994, marking the 50th anniversary of a tragedy involving two Liberator bombers from the 93rd Bomb Group based at Hardwick.

Memorial Erection (1994): The memorial was first erected after a request from an airman who had missed a flight on one of the ill-fated B24 Liberators, as well as money from the Earl of Stradbroke.

A memorial of two inscribed stones now stands at Henham Park, maintained by local volunteers, commemorating all those killed in what became one of the 93rd Bomb Group's deadliest non-combat incidents.
narrative: On 29 March 1944, two B-24 Liberators of the 93rd Bomb Group, based at Hardwick, departed on a bombing mission to the St Nazaire U-boat pens. Over Henham Park in Suffolk, B-24J 42-110033 *Arizona Rambler* and B-24 41-28590 collided in mid-air. The disaster claimed nineteen lives, among them 2nd Lieutenant Max E. Dailey, aged 21. The two aircraft were crewed by McFetrick's crew aboard 41-28590 and Makinster's crew aboard *Arizona Rambler*.
inscription:
[Upright plaque]: OVER THIS AREA ON 29TH MARCH 1944 TWO FULLY ARMED LIBERATOR
BOMBERS FROM THE 93RD BOMB GROUP BASED AT HARDWICK
COLLIDED AND CRASHED ON THE HENHAM PARK ESTATE.
17 AIRMEN FROM THE LIBERATORS DIED IN THE CRASH.
IN THE SUBSEQUENT MASSIVE EXPLOSION OF BOMBS
19 USAAF PERSONNEL FROM RESCUE, MEDICAL AND FIRE FIGHTING UNITS FROM HOLTON AIRFIELD DIED.
THIS MEMORIAL HONOURS THOSE WHO GAVE THEIR LIVES
IN THE CAUSE OF FREEDOM AND MARKS THE ENDURING REGARD IN WHICH THE US 8TH AIR FORCE IS HELD IN EAST ANGLIA.
ERECTED BY THE 8TH EARL OF STRADBROKE 1994
TO MARK THE 50TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE TRAGEDY. [Horizontal plaque]: ROLL OF HONOUR OF THOSE WHO DIED
